title: Duplicate doesn't Duplicate intuitively
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced 4.5 stable, 4.6 beta 1

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21037.1004) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10105F CPU @ 3.70GHz (8 threads) - 15.87 GiB memory

### Issue description

Trying to duplicate a resource completely fails to duplicate it properly, as can be seen when doing a loop load of a scene, and calling duplicate on a resource in the scene and printing the resource after the fact.

The result is a bunch of same IDs when it's expected to have different IDs after duplication, as they're no longer the same resource.

This is due to the expectation that calling duplicate will set the duplicated result as the new resource instead of keeping the old one

I've observed this while trying to make a procedural system for generating some slightly tweaked assets and caching them because runtime duplication was too expensive for the use case, as I'm spamming out new resources every frame dozens of times otherwise.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the MRP and look at the print results.
~~You can play around with what you duplicate and how you duplicate but everything short of making the resource local causes incorrect results, and making the resource local is not the desired solution as that duplicates every time the scene gets instantiated instead of once.~~ 
NVM that part - calling `b.get_child(0).mesh = b.get_child(0).mesh.duplicate(true)` results in the expected behavior vs `b.get_child(0).mesh.duplicate(true)` so this is a documentation issue, as no notes exist about this fact.
